goal: Find the next step of a Perceval fetch from a Discord channel, so a GrimoireLab operator gets every message of the channel they named, and nothing else, without the bot being rate-limited off the guild.

app.name: perceval-discord
app.title: Perceval Discord backend
app.purpose: Decide the next state of the Discord backend's fetch from the state it is in and the last API response: request the channel, page through its messages, finish, refuse a response that breaks the contract, or fail.

fields.name: state
fields.means: where the fetch is: channel (the channel object was requested; every fetch starts here), paging (a page of messages was requested), or a final state

fields.name: response
fields.means: the Discord API v10 response to the last request: ok, foreign (the channel's guild_id is not the guild named), stale (a message not after the cursor), error (401, 403 or 404, or 429 and 5xx after the client's retries)

fields.name: returned
fields.means: messages in the last page; 0 for the channel response

fields.name: limit
fields.means: messages asked for per page, --max-items (Discord's maximum is 100)

fields.name: remaining
fields.means: requests left in the rate-limit bucket, the X-RateLimit-Remaining header

fields.name: floor
fields.means: remaining requests at which the client stops or sleeps, --min-rate-to-sleep

fields.name: sleep
fields.means: whether --sleep-for-rate is given, so an exhausted bucket waits for its reset instead of failing

meanings.channel: the channel object, GET /channels/{channel}, is requested first
meanings.done: every message since from_date was yielded, oldest first
meanings.refused: BackendError: a response broke the API contract or named another guild
meanings.failed: HTTPError or RateLimitError: the token, the bot's permissions, the channel or the rate limit stopped the fetch

rules.why: perceval/backends/core/discord.py: fetch_items returns once the last page is read; a finished fetch is never resumed by the same generator
perceval/client.py: HTTPError and RateLimitError end the fetch
perceval/backends/core/discord.py fetch_items: a channel of another guild raises BackendError
perceval/backends/core/discord.py fetch_items: a page holding a message not after the cursor raises BackendError, so paging cannot loop
perceval/client.py fetch: 401, 403 and 404 raise HTTPError at once; 429 and 5xx raise once MAX_RETRIES (5) retries honoring Retry-After are spent
perceval/backends/core/discord.py fetch_items: a page larger than the limit raises BackendError
perceval/backends/core/discord.py fetch_items: a short page is the last one (Discord API v10, Get Channel Messages)
perceval/client.py sleep_for_rate_limit: without --sleep-for-rate, an exhausted bucket raises RateLimitError before the next request

app.otherwiseWhy: perceval/backends/core/discord.py fetch_items: a full page moves the cursor to its newest message and asks for the next page

properties.why: no message is read from a channel of a guild the operator did not name
a server that ignores the cursor cannot make the fetch run forever
a page larger than asked for is not trusted
the bot never spends the last of its rate-limit bucket, which risks a Discord ban of the guild's bot
no fetch completes without checking the channel's guild and reading its pages
a revoked or under-privileged token, or a missing channel, stops the fetch instead of returning a partial channel as complete

limits: It does not model a response without rate-limit headers: Perceval then never sleeps, as remaining is unknown; give a remaining above floor for it.
It does not model the client's retries: a 429 or 5xx it recovers from is an ok response here, and one it gives up on is error.
It does not decide what a message holds: content, author, attachments and the bot flag pass through unchanged as the item's data.
Edits and deletions after a message was fetched are not refetched: an incremental fetch asks only for messages after the newest one seen.

stakeholders.name: Perceval maintainer
stakeholders.text: Reviews and maintains Perceval's backends for CHAOSS GrimoireLab and needs a new backend that follows the existing ones, adds no dependency, and is tested offline by the suite upstream already runs.

stakeholders.name: GrimoireLab operator
stakeholders.text: Runs Perceval and GrimoireLab for a community and needs every message of the channels they name, resumable from a date and replayable from an archive.

stakeholders.name: Community health analyst
stakeholders.text: Measures CHAOSS metrics such as Chat Platform Inclusivity and needs Discord data in the same item shape as Slack, Mattermost and Rocket.Chat.

stakeholders.name: Discord server admin
stakeholders.text: Adds the read-only bot to the guild and needs it to read only the channels it is granted, with the least permissions, without exhausting the guild's rate limits.

stakeholders.name: Discord member
stakeholders.text: Writes the messages that are collected and needs their content to stay inside the guild's analytics, with bots told apart from people.

stakeholders.name: GrimoireLab security reviewer
stakeholders.text: Triages reports under GrimoireLab's SECURITY.md and needs the bot token never written to an archive or log, and malformed responses refused.

concerns.name: Follows upstream norms
concerns.text: New files only, flake8 clean, a releases/unreleased changelog entry, DCO sign-off, and tests run by tests/run_tests.py with httpretty, as CONTRIBUTING_WITH_CODE.md asks.

concerns.name: Complete channel history
concerns.text: Every message sent at or after from_date is yielded exactly once, oldest first, by paging on the after snowflake.

concerns.name: Least privilege
concerns.text: The bot needs only View Channel, Read Message History and the Message Content intent, and a channel of another guild is refused.

concerns.name: Rate limits respected
concerns.text: The client stops or sleeps at --min-rate-to-sleep and parses Discord's fractional X-RateLimit-Reset.

concerns.name: Token never disclosed
concerns.text: The Authorization header is removed before a request is archived, and the token is never logged.

concerns.name: Refused malformed responses
concerns.text: A page larger than the limit or holding a message not after the cursor raises BackendError instead of looping.

components.name: Discord API v10
components.text: https://discord.com/api/v10: GET /channels/{id} and GET /channels/{id}/messages, authenticated with Authorization: Bot <token>.

components.name: perceval discord
components.text: perceval discord <guild> <channel> -t <token> [--from-date] [--max-items] [--sleep-for-rate] [--min-rate-to-sleep] [--archive-path]: the command DiscordCommand declares.

components.name: Perceval archive
components.text: The SQLite archive Perceval writes with --archive-path and replays with --fetch-archive; requests are stored after sanitize_for_archive.

components.name: GrimoireLab Chronicler
components.text: Turns the backend's items into GrimoireLab CloudEvents (grimoirelab-chronicler, GrimoireLab 2.0).

threats.name: Token written to an archive
threats.text: The bot token in the Authorization header is stored with the archived request and shared with the archive.

control.name: Token removed before archiving
control.text: The archive pickles the whole response, which keeps the sent request with the session's Authorization header, so DiscordClient removes the token from each response before it is archived, and sanitize_for_archive drops it from the archived request; replay works with any token. Found by the live validation's archive check.

evidence.reference: tests/test_discord.py TestDiscordBackendArchive (replayed with a different token)
UOR-Foundation/community oracles/grimoirelab/live: discord.archive.token_free on every live replay probe

threats.name: Channel of another guild read
threats.text: A channel id of a guild the operator did not name is fetched, so data the operator was not asked to analyse is collected.

control.name: Guild checked before paging
control.text: The channel's guild_id must equal the guild named; otherwise BackendError, proved for every request.

threats.name: Endless paging
threats.text: A server or proxy that ignores the after cursor serves the same page forever, so the fetch never ends.

control.name: Cursor must advance
control.text: A page holding a message not after the cursor raises BackendError, proved for every request.

threats.name: Oversized page
threats.text: A response larger than the limit asked for is trusted and processed.

control.name: Page bounded by the limit
control.text: A page larger than --max-items raises BackendError, proved for every request.

threats.name: Bot rate-limited off the guild
threats.text: The fetch keeps requesting with an exhausted bucket and Discord limits or bans the bot for the whole guild.

control.name: Rate gate
control.text: At --min-rate-to-sleep the client sleeps until the bucket resets, taken from X-RateLimit-Reset-After so the local clock cannot skew it (the fractional X-RateLimit-Reset otherwise), or raises RateLimitError, proved for every request; 429 honors Retry-After.

threats.name: Over-privileged bot
threats.text: The bot is granted more than it reads, so a leaked token can post, moderate or read private channels.

control.name: Read-only permissions documented
control.text: The backend only issues GET requests; the documentation asks for View Channel, Read Message History and the Message Content intent and nothing else.

evidence.reference: README.md, Discord section: required bot permissions

threats.name: Deleted messages kept
threats.text: A member deletes a message after it was fetched, and it stays in the operator's archive and indexes.
threats.accepted: Perceval keeps what it fetched for every chat backend; honoring deletions is the operator's duty under Discord's Developer Policy, and the documentation says so.

quality.text: Every message of the fixture channel is yielded exactly once, oldest first, at every page size from 1 to 100.
quality.measureText: Fixture messages not yielded, or yielded twice, by tests/test_discord.py.

quality.text: No archived request holds the Authorization header.
quality.measureText: Archived requests that keep the Authorization header after sanitize_for_archive.

quality.text: Every page that breaks the paging contract ends the fetch with BackendError.
quality.measureText: Oversized or stale pages the fetch continues after.

quality.text: The backend's tests run with no network, inside upstream's tests/run_tests.py.
quality.measureText: Discord tests that fail when every proxy variable is unset.

quality.text: Items carry origin, uuid, updated_on, category and search_fields as Perceval's other chat backends do.
quality.measureText: Item fields of Perceval's Backend contract a Discord item lacks.

brand.name: CHAOSS GrimoireLab

copied.note: The primary CHAOSS logo; media-and-outreach/brand-style-guide.md says the color logo should be used whenever possible.
The secondary reverse white logo the style guide provides, for the dark theme.
The GrimoireLab wizard, the mark docs/_includes/navigation.html shows as the site's navbar brand.

provenance.note: The GrimoireLab site stylesheet: --primary #003756, --secondary #2c3e50, link #003756, link hover #117964, body font Lato, heading font Montserrat, the monospace stack. Not served.
The logo's fills are the CHAOSS palette as exact values: #D50057, #009ADE, #66C9BA, #C19ADE, and #231F20 for the word mark.
The palette as an image: Pantone Rubine Red C, 2925 C, 570 C and Violet 0631 C. Its printed RGB values differ slightly from the logo's fills; the tokens use the fills. Not served.

The CHAOSS brand style guide: CHAOSS in capitals; the color logo whenever possible, reverse white and black where needed; clear space of the diameter of the logo's o; at least 0.75 in (54 px) wide; cite https://chaoss.community. Not served.
Section 8.4: project trademarks are owned by The Linux Foundation; section 7.2 asks participants to respect trademark owners' branding and usage guidelines. Not served.
MIT License, Copyright (c) 2017 chaoss: the license of chaoss/community, which holds the logos.
Apache License 2.0, the license of chaoss/grimoirelab's docs/ (the site, its stylesheet and the wizard). Section 6 grants no permission to use the licensor's trademarks.
GNU GPL 3.0, the license of the rest of chaoss/grimoirelab. Nothing outside docs/ is copied.

tokens.$description: CHAOSS GrimoireLab in W3C DTCG format. color.<name> sets the page variable --<name>; font.<name> sets --font-<name>. A $extensions dark value replaces the color in the dark theme; a color without one keeps the template's dark value.

brand.$description: CHAOSS rubine, the logo's first fill.

ring.$description: CHAOSS blue, the logo's second fill.

sans.$description: GrimoireLab body font stack, docs/css/styles.css. Lato itself is not served.

display.$description: GrimoireLab heading font stack, docs/css/styles.css. Montserrat itself is not served.

license.copied: The CHAOSS logos are from chaoss/community (MIT, Copyright (c) 2017 chaoss); the wizard is from chaoss/grimoirelab docs/ (Apache-2.0). The copyright notices travel with this lock.
license.trademark: CHAOSS is a Linux Foundation project, and its charter (section 8.4) assigns project trademarks to The Linux Foundation. Neither license grants trademark rights (Apache-2.0 section 6 says so). The brand style guide sets how the logo is used but does not grant permission to use it.
license.permission: Not established. Using the CHAOSS name and logos on a page for a contribution to CHAOSS GrimoireLab is the case this lock is built for; any other use, or publishing such a page outside the upstream's own review, needs permission from the CHAOSS project and The Linux Foundation, which has not been asked for or given.

notes: Fonts: GrimoireLab's site loads Lato and Montserrat from Google Fonts (docs/_includes/head.html); neither upstream repository holds their files, and the template's page allows fonts only from itself, so no font is copied and the stacks fall back to installed fonts.
Usage: the style guide asks for clear space of the logo's o and a minimum width of 54 px; the page shows the logo at 6.5rem (104 px) wide with that space around it.

obligations.subject: Commit sign-off
obligations.text: Every commit of the upstream pull request carries Signed-off-by from a person who can certify the DCO, as the CHAOSS Charter and GrimoireLab's CONTRIBUTING_WITH_CODE.md require.
evidence: git log --format=%(trailers:key=Signed-off-by) on the pull request

obligations.subject: Changelog and tests
obligations.text: The change carries a releases/unreleased entry, tests run by upstream's own runner, flake8 clean, and documentation.

obligations.standard: Discord Developer Terms of Service and Developer Policy
obligations.subject: Discord data use
obligations.text: The bot reads only granted channels with GET requests, needs the Message Content intent the server admin enables, and the documentation tells operators to honor deletions.

obligations.subject: Paging and rate limits
obligations.text: Messages are paged with after and limit up to 100, and X-RateLimit-Remaining, fractional X-RateLimit-Reset and Retry-After are honored.

obligations.subject: Vulnerability reporting
obligations.text: Security findings about the backend go through GitHub Security Advisories, never public issues, and the bot token is never archived or logged.

obligations.subject: Participation
obligations.text: The pull request and its discussion follow the CHAOSS Code of Conduct.
